audit.whatIsWrong: Dark Procession is called a 'cage wall' in eight strings and the page never says it can be destroyed.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Yorick summons a DESTRUCTIBLE wall at target location that will block enemy movement', 20/18/16/14/12 seconds, 600 range. That single word is the difference between a lane where a pre-6 Kassadin is helpless inside the cage and one where he has an answer at level 1 — you attack the wall and walk out. The page's whole pre-6 thesis is 'you have no escape until 6', and the wall is precisely where that is least true. Its 20-second cooldown at rank 1 is also the only real gap in Yorick's laning pattern and it is never quoted.
audit.corrected: Dark Procession: 20s at rank 1, 600 range, and the wall is DESTRUCTIBLE — break a segment and walk out. Riftwalk goes over it, but you do not have to wait until 6 for an answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Eulogy of the Isles is referenced four times as 'the Maiden' and its cooldown appears nowhere.
audit.why: It is 160/130/100 seconds at 600 range — the longest cooldown in the matchup by a wide margin, and the single most useful number the page could give. The Maiden is the reason his splitpush threatens a tower and the reason his all-in wins; at 160 seconds at rank 1, a spent Eulogy is nearly three minutes in which he is a melee bruiser with no escape against a blinking assassin. 'Never fight while the Maiden is up' becomes a schedule instead of a warning.
audit.corrected: Eulogy of the Isles: 160s at rank 1, 600 range. Bait it, then own the next two and a half minutes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mourning Mist has no range and no armour shred on the page, and Last Rites is never identified as an auto-attack reset or as a heal.
audit.why: Mourning Mist is 700 range and Riot's text is 'reduces armor, damages, slows and marks enemies. Summoned units gain move speed when moving towards marked targets.' Seven hundred out-reaches your 650 Null Sphere, so 'last-hit at Null Sphere range' is not the safe distance the page presents it as — he pokes you from outside your only pre-6 spell. Last Rites is 6/5.5/5/4.5/4 seconds, carries the auto-reset flag, and heals him: the burst arrives on an attack wind-up rather than a visible cast, and any long trade refills him. Both are flagged interactions and neither is on the page.
audit.corrected: Mourning Mist reaches 700 against your 650 and shreds armour as it marks you. Last Rites is a 6s auto-attack reset that heals him — read the wind-up and keep trades short.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yorick.json (E range 700; Q cooldown 6/5.5/5/4.5/4, autoReset + heal flags)

audit.whatIsWrong: Void Stone's magic reduction is credited with absorbing the ghoul swarm in four places — 'Void Stone's 15% reduction eat the ghoul chip', 'no-sell his ghoul chip', 'his ghouls' magic damage barely scratches you', 'Void Stone's 15% magic reduction shrugs off his ghoul damage'.
audit.why: Riot publishes no damage type for Mist Walkers, so 'their magic damage' is an assertion the files do not support — and the one damage-type signal in Yorick's kit points the other way, since Mourning Mist reduces ARMOUR, which only pays off against physical damage. Rather than replace one unsourced claim with another I removed the attribution and credited the mitigation that is definitely real: Catalyst and Rod of Ages health plus the Null Sphere shield. That keeps the advice (you can absorb the chip once you stall) while dropping the part that might send someone into the wrong resistance.
audit.corrected: Catalyst and Rod of Ages health plus the Null Sphere shield are what let you absorb the ghoul chip. His Mourning Mist shreds armour, which is a hint that raw resistances are the wrong purchase here.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yorick.json (E description; no damage type published for Mist Walkers)

audit.why: Sides and ratings untouched. Yorick owning 1-5, Skill at 6 when Riftwalk answers the cage, and the item stages back to him on Maiden splitpush is exactly what the content whys argue, and whys[6] explicitly closes with 'this last window is his'. The chart and the prose agree here, which is not true of every Kassadin matchup. 71.43% over 7 games is too small to overrule agreement.
Null Sphere interrupts channels and grants a magic-absorbing shield; it has never silenced in this kit version, and silence is a flag the kit builder tracks.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere interrupts channels; it does not silence.

audit.why: 71.43% over 7 games. The page quotes no figure and the sample is thin. No change.

edits.before: Yorick owns levels 1-3 hard — his E (Mourning Mist) slows and marks you so his ghouls dogpile, and his W (Dark Procession) wall can trap you in place, while you have nothing but a mana-hungry Null Sphere and no escape until 6. Do NOT walk up to last-hit when his ghoul stack is full; eat a couple CS losses rather than an E-mark-into-swarm combo that takes a third of your HP. Pop Q for its shield to absorb the ghoul chip when you must step in, and just survive — you have zero kill pressure here and every all-in he forces, he wins.
edits.after: Yorick owns levels 1-3 hard — Mourning Mist reaches 700 against your 650, shredding armour, slowing you and marking you for the ghoul dogpile, and Dark Procession walls you in on a 20s cooldown. But that wall is DESTRUCTIBLE: break a segment and walk out rather than eating the swarm. Last Rites is a 6s auto-attack reset that heals him, so the wind-up is the tell and long trades only refill him. Do NOT step up to last-hit with his ghoul stack full — take the CS loss and hold the Q shield for the step you cannot avoid.

edits.before: Level 6 is your turning point: Riftwalk lets you blink straight over his W cage wall and out of the Maiden + ghoul swarm, so the E-mark all-in that defined your early game stops landing the kill. Once Nether Blade is refunding your mana on-hit and Catalyst/Rod of Ages starts stalling, your Q shield plus Void Stone's 15% magic reduction no-sell his ghoul chip and you trade the lane back from losing to even-plus. Bait him into committing E and his ghoul stack, blink out, then punish the cooldown window — don't fight while his swarm is up.
edits.after: Level 6 is your turning point: Riftwalk blinks you straight over the Dark Procession wall — 20s at rank 1, and destructible if you would rather break it — and out of the Maiden and ghoul swarm, so the E-mark all-in stops landing the kill. Once Nether Blade refunds mana on-hit and Catalyst/Rod of Ages stalls, that health plus your Q shield absorbs the ghoul chip and the lane trades back from losing to even-plus. Eulogy of the Isles is 160s at rank 1 — bait it, blink out, then own that whole window.

edits.before: This is the window you suffered the whole early game to reach. At 2+ items your escalating Riftwalk, ability haste, and Void Stone's 15% magic reduction let you blink-spam onto his squishies and delete them in fights while his ghouls' magic damage barely scratches you — you 1v9 teamfights he can't. The catch: Yorick scales hard as a splitpusher, and his Maiden + ghoul swarm will siege a side tower while you're grouped. Don't try to 1v1 his Maiden push in the side lane — answer it with your roam-and-assassinate tempo and close on his backline instead.
edits.after: This is the window you suffered the whole early game to reach. At 2+ items your escalating Riftwalk, ability haste and Rod of Ages health let you blink-spam onto his squishies and delete them in fights, while a ghoul swarm on foot simply cannot follow a blink — you 1v9 teamfights he can't. The catch: Yorick scales hard as a splitpusher, and the Maiden he gets every 160s at rank 1 will siege a side tower while you're grouped. Don't 1v1 that push — answer it with roam-and-assassinate tempo and close on his backline.

notes: The destructible wall is the biggest practical gain here: the page repeats 'you have no escape until 6' while Riot's own text calls Dark Procession destructible, so a level-2 Kassadin already had an out and was never told. The damage-type question is the one I could not settle — the page asserts four times that the Mist Walkers deal magic damage and that Void Stone therefore absorbs them, and nothing in the kit files gives a damage type for Mist Walkers. I removed the attribution rather than assert 'physical', but the armour shred on Mourning Mist points that way and if it is confirmed then the itemisation advice on this page (and the Void Stone framing on several other Kassadin pages) is pointing readers at the wrong resistance. Logged in unverified. Anti-heal is flagged for Last Rites and does not appear in this page's Itemization row; I did not rewrite an otherwise-correct string to fit it in.
